title: Public identifiers, a published vocabulary and richer structured data
description:
## Why
Search engines and answer engines read schema.org JSON-LD in the page; ours is thin (no identifiers, no "about", no concept data). Vault-LD (assessed 2026-11-13, report at ~/Projects/papyrus-vault-ld-assessment.md) needs exactly what our pages lack: stable identifiers and a shared vocabulary. Ryan approved on 2026-11-13: watch Vault-LD itself, skip it as an authoring/memory/Kanbus format, and pilot the underlying parts. These are the permanent base; any later output (site graph file, Vault-LD copy, SKOS import) reuses them unchanged.

## Scope (pilot, Shipped first)
- A permanent identifier for every public Concept and published Story, built from lineage ids: an id address that never changes and forwards to the current page.
- One Papyrus vocabulary for all sites, published on p.apyr.us, generated from the relation-types file.
- Richer schema.org JSON-LD on pages we already serve: concept pages as defined terms; Story pages naming their concepts by identifier.
- A fixed-field-allowlist privacy test over every linked-data output.

## Decisions (Ryan, 2026-11-13)
1. The words an editor writes on a link stay private.
2. Permanent address = the id address built from the lineage id, forwarding to the page.
3. Linking concepts to outside identifiers (e.g. Wikidata): yes, as a separate story after the pilot.
Defaults accepted: one vocabulary for all sites on p.apyr.us; Shipped is the first site.

## Not in scope
References, a whole-site graph file, any Vault-LD download or output (all left for later).

## Definition of Done
All child stories closed, privacy allowlist test green, and the p.apyr.us documentation task done (every Papyrus feature epic ends with a documentation task on p.apyr.us).

## Priority
Below the in-flight scheduled-publishing/announcements and multilingual epics; board scale P2.
